subject: Commit portfolio alignment & cost-passback proposal
messages:
From: Amit Desai <amit@sovalabs.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@novahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: reserved capacity structure + cost-passback option

Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Sova Labs is ready to move from POC to production across our image and reranking workloads, but we're sensitive to GPU market volatility. We ran a forecast and are proposing a 24-month reserved capacity commitment with a tiered discount schedule plus a limited cost-passback tied to a public GPU pricing index. Key asks: (1) an initial effective discount starting at 16% for the first tranche, (2) an upper bound on passback exposure (cap at 6% of monthly invoice), and (3) a 30‑day liquidity credit during ramp.

Attached: Sova_MA_Pipeline.xlsx (usage forecast, expected peak q4).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the passback with an operational cap, or alternatively offer a guaranteed bridge-credit structure we can rely on if prices spike?

Best,
Amit
Head of Infrastructure, Sova Labs
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Amit Desai <amit@sovalabs.ai>, Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@novahealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 03 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: reserved capacity structure + cost-passback option

Amit — thanks for the clear ask and the forecast. Looping in Kimberly and Karthik to validate structure and approval path. Quick notes from our side: we can do a 24-month reserved with a tiered discount, but passback clauses tied to external indices require a narrow operational definition (index source, lookback window, and cap). Two alternatives we typically offer:

- Passback guardrail: indexation with a monthly cap (your cap request is reasonable) plus a three-month smoothing window.
- Bridge-credit: fixed credit pool (applied first) that covers short-term spikes; credits amortized over initial 6 months of usage.

Karthik — can you run a quick sensitivity against their forecast and propose the discount matrix + exposure cap that finance would accept? Kimberly — once we have the matrix, what's the approval path (exec vs. VP)?

Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Amit Desai <amit@sovalabs.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Mar 2028 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: reserved capacity structure + cost-passback option

Team — I checked Sova's forecast (attached) and ran three GPU-price scenarios: baseline (flat), +25% spike, +50% shock. High level recommendation:

1) Discount matrix: 0-50k GPU-hours/month = 12% discount, 50-200k = 18% discount, >200k = 24% discount (applies to committed baseline).
2) Passback mechanics: use the NY GPU Index (public benchmark) with a 3-month rolling average; cap exposure at 5% of monthly invoice (slightly below Sova's 6% ask).
3) Bridge-credit option: upfront credit equal to 2 months of committed spend, consumed before passback triggers; credits reduce their effective invoice during first quarter.
4) Fallbacks: if index moves >40% over baseline for two consecutive months, Redwood can switch to pre-agreed model-variant (quantized) to reduce unit cost while preserving SLA.

I've attached pricing_scenarios_q1-2028.xlsx with the math. From finance POV, approval to sign with a 5% cap will need VP Commercial sign-off; anything above 5% must go to CRO.

-Karthik
Director, Deal Strategy
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Amit Desai <amit@sovalabs.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Mar 2028 11:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: reserved capacity structure + cost-passback option

Jonas / team —

Thanks Karthik for the scenarios. I support the 24-month commitment with the proposed discount tiers and the 5% cap on passback. A couple of legal and ops notes before we present the finalized offer to Sova: 

- Define index source explicitly in contract (NY GPU Index via third-party provider), include audit right for calculation.
- Add an operational runbook for bridge-credit redemption and automatic model fallback triggers.
- Require monthly usage reporting and a quarterly reconciliation clause.

I'll prepare an approval packet (approval_request_mar23.pdf) to route to VP Commercial; we should target an approval decision by next Wednesday so Jon can send a clean DocuSign. If VP OKs but wants a higher cap, this will need CRO review.

Kimberly Park
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Amit Desai <amit@sovalabs.ai>, Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@novahealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: Sova reserved capacity offer and next steps

Amit / Elena —

Appreciate the patience. Redwood can proceed with the following offer (summary):

- 24-month reserved capacity commitment
- Discount tiers: 12% / 18% / 24% by committed band (applies to baseline committed units)
- Cost-passback: NY GPU Index, 3-month rolling average, 5% monthly cap on passback exposure
- Bridge-credit: upfront credit equal to 2 months committed spend, consumed before any passback collection
- Model fallback: automatic switch to a pre-agreed quantized variant if index rises >40% for 2 months (keeps SLA but reduces unit cost)

Attached: redline_proposal_v1.pdf and the approval packet has cleared VP Commercial (pending CRO note if cap above 5% required). Please review and confirm. If this looks good, I'll send the DocuSign link and legal will populate the index definition and runbook.

Next steps for Sova: sign redline_proposal_v1.pdf and complete procurement worksheet; our finance team will apply bridge-credit at go‑live.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
